missionPremise: P-225 dispatch, live production finding 2026-09-15: Bastrop discrimination across six adjacent Old Town parcels shows SF-1 draws a Polygon (200) while GC/MU parcels 404 'No authoritative setback source covers this district'. Root cause read in code (not inferred): getSetbackTableForZoning (lib/adapters/src/local/setbacks/index.ts) routes every known BDC district to bastrop-development-code, whose table carries only SF-1/SF-2/SF-3/RR rows; mapDistrict (artifacts/api-server/src/lib/buildableEnvelope/districtMapping.ts) then returns null for MU/GC/PDD/etc (first-token exact/prefix match only, never a semantic match), and resolveAuthoritativeSetbacks (authoritativeSetbackSource.ts) short-circuits to null before the atom-chain candidate is ever built -- confirmed by direct read of resolveAuthoritativeSetbacks lines 258-266 (mapDistrict is called and checked for null/fallback-conservative BEFORE any atomCandidate() call exists in the function). This is a census of how widespread that gap-shape is across every onboarded jurisdiction, not a fix.
completionPredicate: A per-district codified/uncodified table for every zoning district in every wired city across the six onboarded counties, each uncodified district carrying exactly one disposition (acquire | serve-from-atom-chain | ruled-out-of-scope) with a cited basis, a parcel count behind each row (live, from the GIS layer's own group-by-count), a total parcel count currently unable to draw an envelope, and the instrument (script) that produced it committed and re-runnable. Falsifiers 1 and 2 (live derive spot-check) run against at least one sampled parcel per disposition class before the census is trusted.
scopeBasis: The six onboarded counties are CONSTRAINT_SEARCH_COUNTIES (artifacts/api-server/src/lib/parcelConstraintSearch.ts:56-62): Bastrop 48021, Caldwell 48055, Hays 48209, McLennan 48309, Travis 48453, Williamson 48491 -- explicitly commented 'the six Central Texas counties the v1 projection covers', corroborated independently by scripts/p85/p85-clerk-portals.mjs's six countyFips seed entries and its own note 'Operator go 2026-08-26: all six counties permitted' (P-85 item 1), and by negative examples in placeCoverageSource.ts and txgioAddressResolveCoverage.test.ts naming Bexar/Bell as OUTSIDE the six-county serving ledger. This is a narrower set than every county with a wired zoning layer: New Braunfels (Comal 48187), San Antonio (Bexar 48029), Seguin + Cibolo (Guadalupe 48187), and Killeen + Belton (Bell 48027) all have live zoning layers and setback tables but sit outside the six -- ruled OUT OF SCOPE BY COUNTY, not counted as uncodified districts in this census. Within the six counties, 'every zoning district' means every distinct district code the city's live public zoning GIS layer actually carries today (per lib/cad-ingest/src/txgio/zoning-layers.ts's ZONING_LAYERS registry, queried live), not the smaller set of codes a setback table happens to name -- a code absent from the GIS layer's live feature set is not a district this product currently sees and is out of scope by construction.

instrumentDesign.approach: Reuse the REAL production resolver (getSetbackTableForZoning + mapDistrict), imported directly from lib/adapters/src/local/setbacks/index.ts and artifacts/api-server/src/lib/buildableEnvelope/districtMapping.ts via tsx (both files have zero runtime external-package imports -- districtMapping.ts's only @workspace/adapters import is `import type`, elided at transpile time -- so they load standalone from a pnpm-uninstalled worktree without a full install). This avoids a second reimplementation of the FIRST-TOKEN match contract per DEV_PROCESS 2.4 ('when one rule has two implementations, the divergence test IS the control' -- importing the one real implementation is stronger than that).
instrumentDesign.liveEnumeration: For each wired city, query its public ArcGIS layerUrl's /query endpoint with groupByFieldsForStatistics=<codeField>&outStatistics=[{count, onStatisticField:<codeField>}] to get every distinct raw code value live on the layer TODAY with its live parcel count, server-side aggregated (verified working against Georgetown's live layer: 17 raw ZONE values with counts, matching the file's own 2026-07-20 comment count of 12 matched + 5 fallback). Apply each city's own codeDomainMap / codeExtractRegex / nullDistrictCodes (all read from the real ZONING_LAYERS registry, not re-typed) to get the canonical stamped code before matching -- this mirrors zoning-stamp.ts's own extraction order (domain-map OR regex, never both in any of the six-county cities, confirmed by reading the registry).
instrumentDesign.instrumentPath: _inbox/2026-09-15_p225_census_instrument.mjs (doc_repo, committed at close) -- takes LDT_ROOT env var (or defaults to a sibling legacy-design-tools checkout) so a future run re-verifies against a fresh worktree.
instrumentDesign.notInstrumentedYet: scripts/surface-probe.mjs's ROWS registry (doc_repo) carries no P-225 predicate -- confirmed by direct read of the full 981-line file (no P-197 or P-225 token present either). probe-close-gate.mjs's own PREDICATE_DEBT set (scripts/enforcement/probe-close-gate.mjs:45-53) already covers P-225 (OPS24_RANGES [200,250]) and ROWS_WITHOUT_PREDICATE includes every PREDICATE_DEBT row, so a close citing a parseable surface-probe.mjs artifact (even one with zero P-225 rows) satisfies the mechanical gate; running surface-probe.mjs --self-test (or a bare run producing a valid instrument=scripts/surface-probe.mjs artifact) supplies that citation. The falsifier spot-checks below are run directly against the live buildable-envelope endpoint (same PE_BASE=https://smartsite.cloud proxy surface-probe.mjs itself uses for envelopeByAddress/envelopeByPoint, which needs no brokerage API key since it goes through the PE proxy, not the brokerage-authenticated route) rather than added as new surface-probe.mjs ROWS entries, since this census produces a per-district table, not a per-parcel pass/fail predicate over a fixed parcel list -- the ontology mismatch is real, not a shortcut; adding a P-225 ROWS entry is out of scope for a census and would be reorder/build-shaped work.

dispositionTaxonomy.acquire: A real codified ordinance/UDC source plausibly exists for the district (conventional Euclidean-looking code, e.g. an R-#/C-#/MF-# family member) but is not yet transcribed into the jurisdiction's SETBACK_TABLES entry. Basis cites the specific city comment or coverage-doc row calling the gap out, or the absence of any code-comment evidence either way (stated as such, not silently defaulted).
dispositionTaxonomy.serveFromAtomChain: A usable per-parcel value already exists in a non-ordinance source the resolver could reach if mapDistrict did not gate it out first. Applied ONLY where I can point at real evidence of that source, which today is Bastrop's own isBdcPerParcelDistrictCode set (MU/GC/PDD/PI/IND/OS, P/OS) per the dispatch's own live-read finding (GIS layer 23 card scalars, served today by the facets route) and authoritativeSetbackSource.ts's atomSourceKind() recognizing a 'layer-23'/'per-parcel'/'onclick' sourceAdapter as gis-per-parcel tier. I have not independently verified an equivalent per-parcel source exists for any other city's gap codes and will not assume one does.
dispositionTaxonomy.ruledOutOfScope: The code is not a conventional Euclidean zoning district this product's dimensional model is built to serve: overlay/combining districts, PUD/planned-development composites, agricultural/conservation/undevelopable, ROW or outside-city-limits sentinels, form-based SmartCode place-types explicitly noted as non-Euclidean, or a repealed/legacy code already superseded on the ground. Basis cites the specific comment calling it form-based/excluded, or the coverage doc's own omission note.

preRegisteredFalsifierAnswers.falsifier1_codifiedDrawsPolygon: Expect PASS on every sampled codified-district parcel. By construction: resolveAuthoritativeSetbacks only returns null when getSetbackTableForZoning returns null OR mapDistrict returns null/fallback-conservative (authoritativeSetbackSource.ts:258-266) -- once a district is 'matched' or 'single', a scalar result is always produced (possibly a disclosed conflict, never a null). A FAIL would mean my read of that gate is wrong, or a parcel-resolution failure unrelated to setback codification (e.g. geocoding) is masquerading as a setback gap.
preRegisteredFalsifierAnswers.falsifier2_uncodified404s: Expect PASS (404 / no-authoritative-source) on every sampled uncodified-district parcel, mirroring the dispatch's own Bastrop GC/MU/PDD measurement. A parcel that instead draws would mean some other path (a different jurisdictionKey resolution, a stale cached bake, a second matching rule) is serving that district and my model of the resolution path is incomplete.
preRegisteredFalsifierAnswers.falsifier3_noZeroCounties: Expect every one of the six counties to show at least one uncodified district -- every wired city's own code comments already name at least one gap code (AG/overlay/PUD-shaped codes appear near-universally). A county returning zero uncodified districts is treated as a signal my enumeration under-counted that county's live GIS codes, not as a clean county, until independently re-checked.

knownFindingsSoFar: legacy-design-tools/AGENTS.md:9-18 states 'if a task mentions Bastrop, municipal data... you are in the wrong repo. Stop' -- STALE relative to the current repo: getSetbackTableForZoning, SETBACK_TABLES, ZONING_LAYERS, and the buildable-envelope route all genuinely live in and are owned by this repo today (verified by direct read at the dispatch's own cited paths), so this is a documentation-staleness finding to report, not a wrong-repo signal to stop on.

docs/property-explorer-setback-coverage-central-tx.md:29 (dated 2026-07-23) claims 'getSetbackTableForZoning resolves every B3 P-* code to bastrop-city-tx' -- STALE against the current code, which routes City-of-Bastrop jurisdiction to bastrop-development-code (current BDC law) and returns null for repealed P-1..P-5/P-CS/P-EC codes (WDLL STEP 3, isRepealedB3PlaceType). A second documentation-staleness finding.

Georgetown's own zoning-layers.ts:22 comment ('Verified live 2026-07-20 for all 12 setback districts (RE/RL/RS/TF/TH/MF-1/MF-2/CN/C-1/C-3/OF/IN)') names 'RL' but georgetown-tx.json's actual district_name rows are RE/RT/RS/RM/TF/TH/MF-1/MF-2/CN/C-1/C-3/OF/IN -- there is no RL row. Live GIS code 'RL' (3 parcels) does NOT match any table row today (confirmed via the real mapDistrict import). Either the comment has always had a typo (RT or RM intended) or the table changed since 2026-07-20; either way the comment is currently wrong and RL is a genuine uncodified gap, not the verified-covered district the comment claims.
